summary.text: 们 is the standardized simplified form of 們. In 們, 亻 is analyzed as the person-related component and 門 as the sound component. Today, 们 marks plurality after pronouns and words for people.

formation.text: The traditional graph 們 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 contributes a person-related category, while 門 supplies a sound cue. This construction describes the graph; it does not explain how the plural-marker meaning arose.

components.text: In 們, 亻 is analyzed as contributing a person-related category.
In 們, 門 is analyzed as the phonetic component. Its modern Mandarin reading mén resembles 們 men, but this comparison does not establish their historical sound relationship.

sound_limitation.text: 門 is reported with Middle Chinese mwon and Old Chinese *mˤə[r] in one reconstruction system, while another source gives *mɯːn in a different system. No corresponding historical reconstruction for 們 is supplied, so these do not establish the historical sound relation.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 門 mén and 們 men share the initial and final, though 們 has a neutral tone. This resemblance is consistent with the reported phonetic analysis but does not prove the historical relationship.

history.text: 們 is represented by 们 in standardized simplified writing, with 門 written as 门. Song-period spellings reported for the suffix include 懣、滿、瞞 and 門; these do not establish a sequence of graphic changes leading to 們.

The seal-style image described in the evidence depicts 門 alone as a modern digital rendering, not an artifact image or an early form of 們. No character-specific early form or graphic sequence for 們 is established.

uncertainties.text: The reported 亻-plus-門 analysis describes the traditional graph 們; its early graphic history is not established here.

Proposed derivations of the plural suffix include links with 輩, 門, 每人, 物 and a Dravidian form. No proposal is established as its source, and no semantic path from these proposals to the plural-marker use is shown.

senses.text: The plural-marker use is reported in Song-period sources; proposed Tang-period evidence is disputed. The exact dated occurrences have not been established in the cited account.

senses.gloss: plural marker used with personal pronouns and person-denoting nouns
senses.text: In modern Chinese, 们 follows personal pronouns or words for people to indicate plurality.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish how any proposed source—輩, 門, 每人, 物 or a Dravidian form—developed into the plural-marker use.

overview.text: 们 is the simplified form of 們 and marks plurality after pronouns and words for people. In 們, 亻 is analyzed as person-related, while 門 provides a sound cue that resembles men in modern Mandarin.

takeaway.text: How the plural-marker meaning arose remains unsettled.
